title: How Much Does a Website Cost in 2026? A Clear Pricing Guide for Small Businesses
summary: Website cost explained: what you pay for a business website, an online store or a custom web app in 2026, what drives the price, hidden costs to plan for and how to get an accurate quote.
body:
"How much does a website cost?" is one of the first questions every business owner asks, and one of the hardest to get a straight answer to. Prices online range from a few dollars a month to six figures. Both can be right, because they describe very different products.

This guide explains what you actually pay for, the typical price ranges for each type of website, the hidden costs most people forget, and how to get a quote you can trust. It is written for small and medium-sized businesses anywhere in the world.

## What you are really paying for

A professional website is not just a design. Behind every good site there are several pieces of work:

- **Strategy**: understanding your clients, your offer and what the site must achieve (calls, quote requests, sales).
- **Design**: page layouts, mobile version, brand consistency and user experience.
- **Development**: turning the design into a fast, secure site, with forms, integrations and an admin area.
- **Content**: texts, images and structure that answer your clients’ questions and help you rank on Google.
- **Technical SEO**: speed, tags, structured data, sitemap and Search Console setup.
- **Launch and support**: hosting, domain, testing, training and updates after go-live.

A cheap website usually skips several of these steps. That is why it costs less, and also why it often brings no clients.

## Typical website prices in 2026

The figures below are common market ranges for work done by a freelancer or a small agency. They vary by country and by the provider’s experience.

| Type of website | Typical budget | Timeline |
|---|---|---|
| DIY site builder (Wix, Squarespace) | $15 – $50 / month + your time | days |
| One-page site or landing page | $500 – $2,500 | 1 – 2 weeks |
| Business website (5 – 15 pages) | $2,000 – $10,000 | 3 – 6 weeks |
| Online store (e-commerce) | $4,000 – $25,000 | 4 – 10 weeks |
| Custom web application | $10,000 and up | 2 – 6 months |

A **business website** is the right choice for most service companies: it presents your offer, builds trust and collects enquiries. An **online store** adds a catalogue, payments, delivery rules and stock management. A **custom web application** (client portal, booking platform, internal tool) is built around your own processes.

## What makes the price go up or down

1. **Number of pages and templates.** Ten pages that share two layouts cost less than ten pages that are all different.
2. **Custom design vs. theme.** A ready-made theme is cheaper; a custom design fits your brand and converts better.
3. **Features.** Booking, payments, multilingual content, client accounts or integrations with your CRM all add development time.
4. **Content.** If you provide finished texts and photos, the price drops. Copywriting and SEO content add to the budget but usually pay for themselves.
5. **Performance and SEO.** A site that loads in under two seconds and is built for search engines takes more care, but it is the one that brings visitors.

## Hidden costs to plan for

- **Domain name**: around $10 – $30 per year.
- **Hosting**: from $0 on modern static hosting to $50+ per month for heavier sites.
- **Maintenance**: updates, backups and security fixes, often $50 – $300 per month.
- **Paid tools or plugins**: forms, booking, e-commerce extensions.
- **Content updates and SEO**: new pages and articles to keep growing your traffic.

Ask every provider what is included after launch. A low build price with expensive or missing maintenance is rarely a bargain.

## Is a cheap website worth it?

A website is an investment only if it brings clients. A $500 site that nobody finds on Google costs more, in lost opportunities, than a well-built site that generates two enquiries a week. The questions to ask are simple:

- Will the site load fast on a phone?
- Is it built so Google can understand and rank it?
- Does every page lead the visitor to a clear action: call, WhatsApp, quote request?
- Can you update it yourself?

If the answer to any of these is no, the price is not the real problem.

## How to get an accurate quote

Before contacting providers, prepare a short brief:

1. Your goal: more leads, online sales, bookings, credibility.
2. The pages you need and three websites you like.
3. The features you need (forms, booking, payments, languages).
4. Who will provide the texts and images.
5. Your budget range and launch date.

With this brief, you can compare quotes on the same basis and avoid surprises.
